passages.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Apollos was in Corinth.
Paul traveled through the inland regions.
Paul came to Ephesus.
Paul found some disciples in Ephesus.
Paul spoke to these disciples.
Paul asked them a question.
Paul said, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?”
The disciples answered Paul.
They said, “No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν Ἀπολλῶ εἶναι ἐν Κορίνθῳ Παῦλον διελθόντα τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εὑρεῖν τινας μαθητάς εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς Εἰ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον ἐλάβετε πιστεύσαντες Οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀλλ’ οὐδ’ εἰ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον ἔστιν ἠκούσαμεν

passages.text: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the disciples in Ephesus.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Into what were you baptized?”
The disciples answered Paul.
They said, “We were baptized into John’s baptism.”
passages.original: Εἶπέν τε Εἰς τί οὖν ἐβαπτίσθητε Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Εἰς τὸ Ἰωάννου βάπτισμα

passages.text: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the disciples in Ephesus.
Paul explained John’s actions.
John baptized people.
John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance.
John told the people to believe in the One who would come after him.
The One who would come after John is Jesus.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Παῦλος Ἰωάννης ἐβάπτισεν βάπτισμα μετανοίας τῷ λαῷ λέγων εἰς τὸν ἐρχόμενον μετ’ αὐτὸν ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The people listened to Paul.
They heard his explanation about Jesus.
They chose to be baptized.
They were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἐβαπτίσθησαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul laid his hands on these men.
The Holy Spirit came upon them.
They spoke in tongues.
They prophesied.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπιθέντος αὐτοῖς τοῦ Παύλου τὰς χεῖρας ἦλθε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτούς ἐλάλουν τε γλώσσαις καὶ ἐπροφήτευον

passages.text: There were about twelve men in all.
passages.sermon:
There were about twelve men in total.
These men heard Paul speak about Jesus.
They believed his message.
They were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Paul laid his hands on them.
The Holy Spirit came upon them.
They spoke in tongues.
They prophesied.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ οἱ πάντες ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ δώδεκα

passages.text: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul entered the synagogue.
He spoke boldly in the synagogue.
He did this for three months.
He argued about the kingdom of God.
He persuaded people about the kingdom of God.
passages.original: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἐπαρρησιάζετο ἐπὶ μῆνας τρεῖς διαλεγόμενος καὶ πείθων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher.
Some people in the synagogue refused to believe.
They became stubborn.
They spoke badly about the Way in front of everyone.
Paul separated himself from these people.
He took his disciples with him.
Paul left the synagogue.
He spoke every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
passages.original: ὡς δέ τινες ἐσκληρύνοντο καὶ ἠπείθουν κακολογοῦντες τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πλήθους ἀποστὰς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀφώρισεν τοὺς μαθητάς καθ’ ἡμέραν διαλεγόμενος ἐν τῇ σχολῇ Τυράννου

passages.text: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul taught in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
He did this every day.
He continued for two years.
Everyone who lived in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord.
Both Jews and Greeks heard it.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ ἔτη δύο ὥστε πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν Ἀσίαν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας

passages.text: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul, so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
passages.sermon:
God did miracles through Paul.
These miracles were not ordinary.
God used Paul’s hands to do these miracles.
People took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul’s skin.
They brought these cloths to sick people.
When the sick people received the cloths, their diseases left them.
Evil spirits also left them.
passages.original: Δυνάμεις τε οὐ τὰς τυχούσας ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίει διὰ τῶν χειρῶν Παύλου ὥστε καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ἀποφέρεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ σουδάρια ἢ σιμικίνθια καὶ ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι ἀπ’ αὐτῶν τὰς νόσους τά τε πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκπορεύεσθαι

passages.text: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I bind you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
passages.sermon:
Some Jewish exorcists traveled from place to place.
They tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus.
They spoke this name over people who had evil spirits.
They said, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
passages.original: Ἐπεχείρησαν δέ τινες καὶ τῶν περιερχομένων Ἰουδαίων ἐξορκιστῶν ὀνομάζειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Ὁρκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν Παῦλος κηρύσσει

passages.text: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
passages.sermon:
Sceva was a Jewish chief priest.
He had seven sons.
These seven sons tried to use the name of Jesus to cast out evil spirits.
They did what the other Jewish exorcists were doing.
passages.original: ἦσαν δέ τινος Σκευᾶ Ἰουδαίου ἀρχιερέως ἑπτὰ υἱοὶ τοῦτο ποιοῦντες

passages.text: Eventually, one of the evil spirits answered them, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
passages.sermon:
An evil spirit spoke to the men.
The spirit said, “I know Jesus.”
The spirit said, “I know about Paul.”
The spirit said, “But who are you?”
passages.original: ἀποκριθὲν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τὸν Μὲν Ἰησοῦν γινώσκω καὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἐπίσταμαι ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνες ἐστέ

passages.text: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
passages.sermon:
A man had an evil spirit inside him.
This man jumped on the seven sons of Sceva.
He attacked all of them.
He was stronger than all of them.
He overpowered them.
They could not defend themselves.
They ran out of the house.
They were naked.
They were wounded.
passages.original: καὶ ἐφαλόμενος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἐν ᾧ ἦν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν κατακυριεύσας ἀμφοτέρων ἴσχυσεν κατ’ αὐτῶν ὥστε γυμνοὺς καὶ τετραυματισμένους ἐκφυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου ἐκείνου

passages.text: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
passages.sermon:
All the Jews living in Ephesus heard about this.
All the Greeks living in Ephesus heard about this.
Everyone in Ephesus learned what happened.
Fear came over all of them.
People respected the name of the Lord Jesus.
People honored the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο γνωστὸν πᾶσιν Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν Ἔφεσον καὶ ἐπέπεσεν φόβος ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς καὶ ἐμεγαλύνετο τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
passages.sermon:
Many people had believed in Jesus.
These believers came forward.
They confessed their sins.
They openly told about what they had done.
passages.original: πολλοί τε τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἤρχοντο ἐξομολογούμενοι καὶ ἀναγγέλλοντες τὰς πράξεις αὐτῶν

passages.text: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
passages.sermon:
Some people in Ephesus had practiced magic arts.
These people brought their books about magic.
They burned these books in front of everyone.
They counted the value of the books.
The total value was fifty thousand drachmas.
passages.original: ἱκανοὶ δὲ τῶν τὰ περίεργα πραξάντων συνενέγκαντες τὰς βίβλους κατέκαιον ἐνώπιον πάντων καὶ συνεψήφισαν τὰς τιμὰς αὐτῶν καὶ εὗρον ἀργυρίου μυριάδας πέντε

passages.text: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
passages.sermon:
The word of the Lord spread.
The word of the Lord grew strong.
The Lord gave the word great power.
The word of the Lord prevailed everywhere.
passages.original: Οὕτως κατὰ κράτος τοῦ Κυρίου ὁ λόγος ηὔξανεν καὶ ἴσχυεν

passages.text: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul made a decision in his spirit.
He decided to travel to Jerusalem.
He planned to go through Macedonia and Achaia first.
Paul said, “After I have been in Jerusalem, I must also see Rome.”
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληρώθη ταῦτα ἔθετο ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῷ πνεύματι διελθὼν τὴν Μακεδονίαν καὶ Ἀχαΐαν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰπὼν ὅτι Μετὰ τὸ γενέσθαι με ἐκεῖ δεῖ με καὶ Ῥώμην ἰδεῖν

passages.text: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian leader and apostle.
Paul had helpers who served with him.
Paul sent two helpers to Macedonia.
Their names were Timothy and Erastus.
Paul did not go with them.
Paul stayed for a time in Asia.
passages.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ εἰς τὴν Μακεδονίαν δύο τῶν διακονούντων αὐτῷ Τιμόθεον καὶ Ἔραστον αὐτὸς ἐπέσχεν χρόνον εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν

passages.text: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
passages.sermon:
At that time, a great disturbance happened.
This disturbance was about the Way.
The Way means the Christian faith.
Many people were upset because of the Christian message.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος περὶ τῆς Ὁδοῦ

passages.text: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.
passages.sermon:
A man named Demetrius lived in Ephesus.
Demetrius worked as a silversmith.
He made silver shrines of the goddess Artemis.
He gave much business to the craftsmen.
Many craftsmen depended on Demetrius for their work.
passages.original: Δημήτριος γάρ τις ὀνόματι ἀργυροκόπος ποιῶν ναοὺς ἀργυροῦς Ἀρτέμιδος παρείχετο τοῖς τεχνίταις οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐργασίαν

passages.text: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.
passages.sermon:
Demetrius was a silversmith.
He made silver shrines of Artemis.
He brought much business to the craftsmen.
Demetrius gathered the craftsmen together.
He also gathered the workmen in related trades.
Demetrius spoke to them.
He said, “Men, you know this business gives us prosperity.”
passages.original: οὓς συναθροίσας καὶ τοὺς περὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργάτας εἶπεν Ἄνδρες ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ἐργασίας ἡ εὐπορία ἡμῖν ἐστιν

passages.text: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a preacher.
Paul teaches in Ephesus.
Paul also teaches in almost all of Asia.
You can see this.
You can hear this.
Paul has persuaded many people.
Paul has turned a large crowd away from idols.
Paul says, “Gods made by human hands are not gods.”
passages.original: καὶ θεωρεῖτε καὶ ἀκούετε ὅτι οὐ μόνον Ἐφέσου ἀλλὰ σχεδὸν πάσης τῆς Ἀσίας ὁ Παῦλος οὗτος πείσας μετέστησεν ἱκανὸν ὄχλον λέγων ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοὶ οἱ διὰ χειρῶν γινόμενοι

passages.text: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”
passages.sermon:
Demetrius spoke to the craftsmen and workmen in Ephesus.
He warned them about a danger.
He said our business might lose its good reputation.
He also said the temple of the great goddess Artemis might be dishonored.
He said Artemis might lose her majesty.
All Asia and the whole world worship Artemis.
passages.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο κινδυνεύει ἡμῖν τὸ μέρος εἰς ἀπελεγμὸν ἐλθεῖν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τῆς μεγάλης θεᾶς Ἀρτέμιδος ἱερὸν εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι μέλλειν τε καὶ καθαιρεῖσθαι τῆς μεγαλειότητος αὐτῆς ἣν ὅλη ἡ Ἀσία καὶ ἡ οἰκουμένη σέβεται

passages.text: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
passages.sermon:
The men heard these words.
They became very angry.
They began to shout loudly.
They said, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ καὶ γενόμενοι πλήρεις θυμοῦ ἔκραζον λέγοντες Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων

passages.text: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
The whole city became confused.
People acted together with one purpose.
They rushed into the theatre.
They seized Gaius and Aristarchus.
Gaius and Aristarchus were from Macedonia.
Gaius and Aristarchus traveled with Paul.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ πόλις τῆς συγχύσεως ὥρμησάν τε ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον συναρπάσαντες Γάϊον καὶ Ἀρίσταρχον Μακεδόνας συνεκδήμους Παύλου

passages.text: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a leader among the Christians.
Paul wanted to go before the assembly.
The disciples were his followers.
The disciples did not allow Paul to go before the assembly.
passages.original: Παύλου δὲ βουλομένου εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον οὐκ εἴων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταί

passages.text: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
passages.sermon:
Paul had friends who were officials in the province of Asia.
These officials cared about Paul.
They sent a message to Paul.
They begged Paul not to go into the theatre.
passages.original: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἀσιαρχῶν ὄντες αὐτῷ φίλοι πέμψαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παρεκάλουν μὴ δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον

passages.text: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
passages.sermon:
The assembly was in turmoil.
People were confused.
Some people shouted one thing.
Other people shouted something different.
Most people did not know why they had gathered.
passages.original: Ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν ἄλλο τι ἔκραζον ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἐκκλησία συγκεχυμένη καὶ οἱ πλείους οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τίνος ἕνεκα συνεληλύθεισαν

passages.text: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward to explain himself, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.
passages.sermon:
The crowd was large and confused.
Some Jews were in the crowd.
These Jews pushed Alexander forward.
Alexander was a Jew.
Alexander wanted to explain himself to the people.
He raised his hand.
He motioned for silence.
He wanted to make his defense to the people.
passages.original: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ὄχλου συνεβίβασαν Ἀλέξανδρον προβαλόντων αὐτὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος κατασείσας τὴν χεῖρα ἤθελεν ἀπολογεῖσθαι τῷ δήμῳ

passages.text: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
passages.sermon:
The crowd saw Alexander.
They understood that Alexander was a Jew.
Everyone in the crowd began to shout together.
They shouted for about two hours.
They said, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
passages.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κραζόντων Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων

passages.text: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
passages.sermon:
The city clerk stood before the crowd.
He quieted the people.
He spoke to the people of Ephesus.
He said, “Men of Ephesus, listen.
Everyone knows this city.
Ephesus is the guardian of the temple of the great Artemis.
Ephesus also guards the image of Artemis that fell from heaven.”
passages.original: Καταστείλας δὲ ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον φησίν Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς

passages.text: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.
passages.sermon: These facts are undeniable.\r\nYou must remain calm.\r\nYou must not do anything rash.
passages.original: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν

passages.text: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.
passages.sermon: You brought these men here.\r\nThese men did not rob our temple.\r\nThese men did not blaspheme our goddess.
passages.original: ἠγάγετε γὰρ τοὺς ἄνδρας τούτους οὔτε ἱεροσύλους οὔτε βλασφημοῦντας τὴν θεὸν ἡμῶν

passages.text: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
passages.sermon:
Demetrius is a craftsman.
He has fellow craftsmen with him.
If Demetrius and these craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, they should use the courts.
The courts are open.
Proconsuls are available.
Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen should bring charges against one another in the courts.
passages.original: Εἰ μὲν οὖν Δημήτριος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεχνῖται ἔχουσι πρός τινα λόγον ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται καὶ ἀνθύπατοί εἰσιν ἐγκαλείτωσαν ἀλλήλοις

passages.text: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.
passages.sermon:
If you want something more than this,
You must settle it in a legal assembly.
The law requires this process.
You cannot resolve it outside the proper assembly.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τι περαιτέρω ἐπιζητεῖτε ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐπιλυθήσεται

passages.text: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”
passages.sermon:
We are in danger today.
Someone may accuse us of causing a riot.
There is no real reason for this disturbance.
We cannot give any explanation for this commotion.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ἀποδοῦναι λόγον περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης

passages.text: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
passages.sermon:
A city official spoke to the crowd in Ephesus.
He warned them about the danger of being charged with rioting.
He told them that any further issues must be settled in a legal assembly.
After he finished speaking, he dismissed the assembly.
The people left the gathering.
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν
